Apple's commercial secrets lawsuit against OpenAI has been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, replacing the magistrate judge who was originally assigned to the case. Here's the details.

Following the assignment of the new judge, the original October hearing has been cancelled

When a civil lawsuit is filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, it is randomly assigned to a U.S. district judge or a magistrate judge. If the case is assigned to a magistrate judge, all parties involved need to indicate whether they consent to the judge having full authority to preside over the case.

This is because U.S. district judges have the authority to preside over federal civil cases from start to finish, while magistrate judges can only do so if all parties consent.

On the day Apple filed its commercial secrets lawsuit against two former employees, OpenAI, and Jony Ive's io Products, the case was randomly assigned to Magistrate Judge Virginia K. DeMarchi.

This means all parties involved in the lawsuit need to submit a form indicating whether they consent to DeMarchi having full authority to preside over the case.

Apple appears to have refused this arrangement. Yesterday the company submitted a 'consent or refusal' form (which has not yet been made public), and that form appears to have triggered the process of reassigning the case to a U.S. district judge.

The inability to see other documents explaining this reassignment strongly suggests Apple chose to refuse to have the magistrate judge preside over the case.

As a result, the case has now been reassigned to U.S. District Judge Edward Davila, with Magistrate Judge Nathanael Cousins handling discovery-related matters.

Following the reassignment, the initial case management conference originally scheduled before Judge DeMarchi on October 13 has been cancelled and needs to be rescheduled before Judge Davila.

However, two other sets of deadlines remain in effect: parties must discuss settlement proposals and a discovery plan by September 22, then submit initial disclosures and jointly submit a joint case management statement by October 6.
